account: A 22-year-old Brazilian woman in Japan had had type 1 diabetes for 11 years. She miscarried at 7 and 9 weeks in two earlier pregnancies, when she used a MiniMed 620G sensor-augmented pump without predictive low glucose suspend. At about 6 weeks of her third pregnancy she was switched to a Medtronic MiniMed 640G sensor-augmented pump with predictive low glucose suspend. The pump suspended insulin for about 249 minutes per day. Her hypoglycemic episodes fell from 2.1–2.5 to 1.4 per day, and time below 70 mg/dL fell from 1.1–1.4% to 0.5%. She delivered a 4,137 g boy by cesarean section at 39 weeks and 3 days with no significant complications. After the delivery she went back to multiple daily injections at her own request, and her glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) stayed at 5 to 6% while she breastfed. Clinicians at the University of Toyama described the case in Diabetology International on 6 March 2021, without event dates. In a study published on 30 March 2024, clinicians in Tokyo with no connection to the case reported that 11 pregnant women on the same pump reached glucose targets without more hypoglycemia. They state that the pump was launched in Japan in 2018.

Obstetric and diabetes care were delivered by clinicians. The causal link to carrying the pregnancy is inferred, not demonstrated.

fields.account: A 22-year-old Brazilian woman in Japan had had type 1 diabetes for 11 years. She miscarried at 7 and 9 weeks in two earlier pregnancies, when she used a MiniMed 620G sensor-augmented pump without predictive low glucose suspend. At about 6 weeks of her third pregnancy she was switched to a Medtronic MiniMed 640G sensor-augmented pump with predictive low glucose suspend. The pump suspended insulin for about 249 minutes per day. Her hypoglycemic episodes fell from 2.1–2.5 to 1.4 per day, and time below 70 mg/dL fell from 1.1–1.4% to 0.5%. She delivered a 4,137 g boy by cesarean section at 39 weeks and 3 days with no significant complications. After the delivery she went back to multiple daily injections at her own request, and her glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) stayed at 5 to 6% while she breastfed. Clinicians at the University of Toyama described the case in Diabetology International on 6 March 2021, without event dates. In a study published on 30 March 2024, clinicians in Tokyo with no connection to the case reported that 11 pregnant women on the same pump reached glucose targets without more hypoglycemia. They state that the pump was launched in Japan in 2018.
